title: compact-response-allocator-proto-prd
content:
Rough PRD / idea dump: Compact Response Allocator (CRA)

Context / problem:
- Teams want predictable token costs per user action but also need high utility in the important cases. Current approaches (fixed model selection, blunt truncation) either waste tokens or degrade UX unpredictably.
- We have primitives that help (caching, model variants, quantization) but no unified way to allocate a per-response token budget with graceful, quality-aware compression.

High-level thesis:
- Provide an allocator that accepts a per-request budget hint (or infers one) and produces responses that trade off verbosity vs. fidelity in structured, observable steps. The allocator combines: lightweight compression transforms, fidelity tiers, selective regeneration, and post-hoc stitching so callers get usable content while we control token spend.

Goals (measurable):
1) Reduce median tokens-per-response for chat-like flows by 25% on experimental workloads without decreasing helpfulness score > 3% (micro-evals).
2) Offer predictable 50th/95th percentile token ceilings for API customers on configured budgets.
3) Provide telemetry hooks so customers see where token savings came from (compression, truncation, cached fragments, model downgrade).

Core concepts / vocabulary:
- budget_hint: optional param (tokens/byte-equivalent or tier name) sent by caller or inferred by policy.
- fidelity_knob: ordered set of transforms (lossless rewrite -> compact paraphrase -> extractive summary -> short form -> model downgrade).
- response_strata: composition of fragments labelled by fidelity level (primary answer, supporting context, provenance).
- stitching: deterministic reassembly of compressed fragments + indicators so clients can re-expand or request full version.
- grace-fallback: if compressed output fails quality checks, automatically escalate to a higher-fidelity transform or re-run with larger budget.

API sketch (proto):
- request fields: budget_hint (int or enum), compression_profile (id), allow_stitching (bool), debug_trace (bool).
- response: text + compact_annotations (list of tokens saved per transform), fidelity_level, original_token_estimate, final_token_count, expansion_handle (opaque id if full available).

User stories:
- As a product engineer, I can set a budget_hint for a route so heavy routes (search-summaries) use aggressive compression while conversational routes use relaxed defaults.
- As an enterprise customer, I can enable per-organization profiles so compliance teams can opt for lossless-only transforms.
- As an SDK user, I can call .expand(handle) to get a full unfurled version (consumes tokens) if I need to show full details.

Transforms / heuristics (brainstorm):
- prefix-preserving compression: remove internal filler while keeping opening/closing lines to preserve apparent coherence.
- zipper summarization: interleave extractive snippets with compressed paraphrases to keep salient facts while cutting fluff.
- delta encoding for multi-turn: send only deltas from previously cached assistant message (works with session cache).
- structured extraction: detect lists/tables and compress into short bullet IDs with lookup mapping for full expansion.
- inline links to expansion_handle for provenance blocks (keeps visible trace but moves tokens to expandable payload).

Safety / quality checks:
- micro-eval classifier that rejects compressed outputs that drop required entities/negate meaning.
- NLI-based sanity check to detect contradiction between compressed and original candidate.
- per-customer policy layer to prevent compression of legally required disclaimers.

Telemetry & metrics:
- tokens_saved_by_transform (map per transform id)
- helpfulness_score_delta (micro-eval pre/post)
- expansion_rate (how often clients call expand(handle))
- p95_token_after_compression per route/profile
- incidents where grace-fallback triggered and reason codes

Operational model / infra considerations: 
- Runtime needs fast lightweight transforms pre- or post-decoding. Prefer post-generation compression (operate on text) to avoid complex kernel-level changes.
- For delta encoding, rely on existing session KV store + sha256 of last assistant message to compute diffs.
- Expansion payloads stored in short-term object storage with TTL (configurable per-org) and access controlled by API key.
- Cache-friendly: store compressed fragments in shared cache keyed by (session, fragment-hash, profile).

Rollout plan (staged):
1) Lab prototype: implement 3 simple transforms (extractive summary, paraphrase compress, delta-of-last). Evaluation harness against internal datasets (2 weeks).
2) Canary: expose as opt-in param for 5 teams (internal & selected customers). Monitor helpfulness and token metrics for 6 weeks.
3) Public beta: make budget_hint available for hosted routes and console toggles for profiles.
4) GA: add SDK helpers, console insights, enterprise policy exceptions.

Experiment matrix (examples):
- Aggressiveness levels (none, mild, medium, aggressive) x route type (chat, qa, summarization) x model tier (gpt-like, open-llama). Metrics: tokens per resp, helpfulness, latency delta.

UX / Console:
- Per-route slider to set default budget_hint and preview expected token savings with live sample prompts.
- Expansion audit view showing top expand calls and per-customer cost impact.

Open questions / risks: 
- How to measure "helpfulness" at scale cheaply? (micro-evals vs user telemetry)
- Privacy/compliance: storing expansion payloads may be sensitive. Need per-org TTL and optional disable.
- Latency tradeoffs: some transforms (paraphrase) add CPU/decoding cost; need to model net unit cost.
- API complexity: how many knobs is too many? Start simple.

Immediate next steps (for me):
- Spike: implement extractive-summary -> paraphrase pipeline as a post-generator transform in the sandbox runtime (NOAH + MILES to help). Target: 1 week.
- Create evaluation set: 500 multi-turn chats across enterprise and consumer verticals. Build micro-eval harness (PRIO: helpfulness classifier).
- Draft SDK param shapes and console preview mockups (Priya to help with UX notes).
- Add JIRA ticket skeleton (PLAT-1987) and a small RFC for platform owners.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Might call the feature "stitchable-compact-answers" in UI to avoid jargon.
- Consider per-customer cost-savings report with projected savings if enabled at X aggressiveness.
- Could combine with Optimize recommendations to suggest profiles for routes with high token waste.

Edge example (toy):
Request: summarise last 30 messages; budget_hint=120 tokens; allow_stitching=true
Candidate flow:
1) Run full generator unconstrained -> 600 tokens candidate (internal only).
2) Extractive summary -> 140 tokens (keeps all entities)
3) Paraphrase compress -> 95 tokens (passes NLI check) -> returned to customer with expansion_handle storing full 600-token payload for later.
Telemetry: tokens_saved=505, fidelity_level=paraphrase, expansion_available=true

TODO checklist:
- [ ] Spike transforms in sandbox runtime
- [ ] Build micro-eval harness + dataset
- [ ] Design simple API shape and SDK helpers
- [ ] Console preview mockups + Per-route defaults
- [ ] Security review for expansion storage
- [ ] Pricing experiments with finance (savings pass-through?)

End of brain dump. Need to tidy into a proper PRD if spike results look promising.
